newsitem.title: POLAND: WARSAW BOURSE HITS HIGH AMONG EAST EUROPE MARKET.
newsitem.headline: WARSAW BOURSE HITS HIGH AMONG EAST EUROPE MARKET.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange led
mixed trading on East European markets this week, surging to a
30-month high before retreating on a round of profit-taking.
Shares in Zagreb also hit new highs, while the Budapest,
Bratislava, Ljubljana and Romanian bourses edged up slightly
and Prague lost ground. Bulgarian markets held steady.
WARSAW
The Warsaw Stock Exchange soared this week, setting a
30-month high before falling on Thursday and Friday, but
analysts said it was likely to return to the uptrend next week.
"It's likely the market will go up again, but the question
is how far and how long it will rise", said Remigiusz Tarka, an
analyst at IB Austria brokerage.
Some analysts said the main WIG index could rise to about
16,000 points in the next few weeks but said that a deeper
correction afterwards was possible due to the bourse's rise by
over 90 percent since the beginning of the year.
The WIG index closed at 14,504.1 on Thursday, up 1.5
percent from last Friday's close.
BUDAPEST
The Budapest bourse edged up in flat trading this week, as
investors waited on the sidelines to see if the U.S. Federal
Reserve would raise interest rates next week.
The BUX index closed on Friday at 3,550.20 points, up 17.11
from Monday's open.
"The wait-and-see attitude of the market has remained
unchanged. Since news of a potential rate hike in the U.S. was
released, the market has been stagnant," Peter Lencs of MKB
Securities said.
Recent macroeconomic data failed to have a major impact on
trading while corporate results slowed to a trickle, although
plastics company Pannonplast announced a capital increase at
three of its units.
PRAGUE
Czech shares lost ground over the week after the central
bank placed the country's fifth largest bank, Agrobanka, under
temporary forced administration due to liquidity problems,
leaving some investors jittery.
The PX50 index closed Friday's session at 565.8, off eight
points for the week.
Savings bank Ceska Sporitelna was indicative of the
market's mood, showing heavy volatility, hitting a year high
and then falling sharply.
Sporitelna particularly has been the subject of uncertainty
because of the relatively large stake in the bank held by
investment firm Motoinvest which was also heavily involved with
Agrobanka.
"There are lots of rumours around the market with
Motoinvest and no body could really tell you what the real
situation is," said Robert Sekete a trader at brokerage Wood &
Company. Agrobanka shares fell about 25 percent from Monday to
close at 87.09 crowns on Friday.
BRATISLAVA
Slovak blue chip shares saw a week of listless trading on
the Bratislava Stock Exchange, with further financial issues
continuing to show weakness.
The 12-share SAX index held steady for the most part,
closing on Friday at 208.68 points, up slightly from Monday's
open of 208.65.
Analysts said they expected lower volumes of traded stocks
to result in a further decline in prices in general. "We don't
expect any stronger impulse leading to a significant revival of
activity on the market," said Libor Chrast of ING Barings.
BULGARIA
No corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market
this week, as brokers and investors focused on other
investments. The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index
(RABSI) closed at 41.14 points, unchanged from last Thursday.
"Investors are shying away from the stock market and
focusing their attention on government securities and foreign
currency, which are more liquid and offer higher yields," one
broker said.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks forged ahead this week with two upswings to
hit all-time highs, leaving traders optimistic that the bull
run could be sustained due to several positive factors.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka, which was the most-actively
traded, jumped 150 kuna to 900 and pharmaceuticals group Pliva
rose to 13,000 kuna from last Friday's 12,200 to lead the way.
Another popular issue, confectioner Kras, gained 80 kuna
amid rumours that the EBRD was close to buying into the firm.
But Kras denied rumours any kind of deal was imminent.
BUCHAREST
Bucharest shares traded mixed early in the week, drifting
lower on Thursday amid thin investor interest.
Azomures SA fertiliser maker held centre stage, but closed
the week 500 lei softer at 10,700.
The Bucharest stock exchange will not trade next week as it
installs new software to improve trading and settlement.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares started to recuperate slowly following the
last week's slump to an all-time low as the market started to
build optimism on the successful listing of a new issue of
shares of drug maker Lek.
"The good performance of last week's listing of Lek's A
issue brought optimism to the market and could fuel growth over
the next week," one trader said. The SBI index closed on Friday
at 918.86, down 6.86 points on the week.
